To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the flow field in the diffuser depends on the J factor and that the flow distribution within the monolith is a function of the J factor and the Reynolds number.
pulsating flow in a wide-angle diffuser can result in a flow field that resembles a steady flow field.

the flow distribution across automotive catalyst monolith placed downstream of a planar diffusers presented with pulsating exhaust flow is a strong function of the ratio of pulse period (frequency) to residence time within diffuser (J factor).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of a new experimental facility to study flow distribution within automotive exhaust catalysts.
the development of an understanding of flow distribution in a pulsating exhaust flow.
the effect of pulsating flow on the flow distribution across automotive catalyst monolith.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
increasing J results in greater flow maling and greater flow maldistributions.

pulsating flow in a diffuser with J < 6.8 results in flow fields that are very similar to those produced by steady flow at the same Re, with the flow distribution in the monoliths being very dependent on the J factor.
pulsating flow in the diffuser upstream of the catalyst monoliths has little influence on the flow distribution within the catalyst monolith.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the flow distribution within a monolith is dependent upon both the J factor and Reynolds number, the latter being more important at higher J. The
pulsating flow is beneficial in reducing flow maldistribution across the monoliths.
for a given Re, the J factor determines the extent of flow separation and the degree of flow maldistribution in the monolith.
The main takeaway from our work is that
flow maldistribution can be reduced with a diffuser of the same angle but of a larger width.
pulsating flow can be beneficial for the catalyst performance, but this depends on the pulsation frequency.
the J factor is a useful parameter for describing flow separation in a planar wide-angle diffuser.
